summary: Model updated for the NEWLEADER/UPTODATE reordering; two committed-data-loss defects remain in the updated learner sync path (one reproduced).
validation_limits: Model checking is budget-limited (LIMITED_COVERAGE): standard MC.cfg BFS reached depth 42 (43.2M distinct states) with a nonempty queue; no run is an exhaustive proof.
SyncTrunc is not observed in any fresh implementation trace; its reachability rests on a model canary only.
MC-1's loss consequence needs a process crash inside the observed ACK-before-fsync window; it was not reproduced in-JVM (window observed on real traces).
JDK 21 only (as in V0); the specula ci-result command is not installed in this environment, so generated CI reports were not produced.

findings.title: Learner failure between NEWLEADER and UPTODATE hides logged committed records
findings.cause: An updated learner's server is INITIAL between NEWLEADER and UPTODATE and applies DIFF records only after UPTODATE; on failure in between, canShutdown() is false so the data tree is never fast-forwarded, and the FLE vote and a new leader's loaded database omit the records.
findings.trigger: Leader activates on NEWLEADER ACKs from learners that then fail before UPTODATE (socket timeout or leader loss) without a process restart; the learners elect a new leader among themselves.
findings.consequence: A transaction already served as committed by the previous leader is missing from the new leader's database (data inconsistency, no crash required).

premises: The learner fails after its NEWLEADER ACK and before UPTODATE without the process restarting.
The FLE vote and leader database use the in-memory data tree (QuorumPeer.getLastLoggedZxid, ZooKeeperServer.loadData).

findings.title: NEWLEADER ACK precedes durability of synchronized records
findings.cause: The updated NEWLEADER branch persists the new epoch, enqueues the DIFF records to the asynchronous SyncRequestProcessor via logRequest, and writes the NEWLEADER ACK before they are forced; the leader commits and serves its whole history on that ACK quorum.
findings.trigger: A learner that acknowledged NEWLEADER crashes (process/power failure) before its SyncThread forces the DIFF records, then restarts with the new epoch and wins the next election.
findings.consequence: Committed history is persisted on fewer than a quorum (observed on real traces) and, after the crash, a transaction already served as committed is lost from the next leader's history.

premises: Fail-stop crash loses queued and appended-but-unforced transaction-log records.
In-JVM tests cannot kill a single peer between the NEWLEADER ACK and the SyncThread flush (environment limitation).
